quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ling Hai (about a month in the role): 'In the first 4 weeks of August, broadly, all the operating metrics are in line with the first 4 weeks in July', including cross-border travel and non-travel on a like-for-like basis; the macro environment remains supportive of consumer and business spend across affluent and mass consumers. The Middle East hit inbound and outbound travel in April, but year to date the impact is 'much less negative than we expected', with travellers shifting routes rather than stopping; cross-border card-not-present growth also comes from new categories such as AI subscriptions on card on file (her example: Perplexity AI), crypto purchases out of Venezuela and wallet funding (Revolut, Wise).

CFO Ling Hai: Mastercard closed the BVNK acquisition on August 3; BVNK is an orchestration layer that gives Mastercard a white-label wallet (offered through its customers) to store, convert, receive and send stablecoins and interoperability across stablecoins, blockchains and fiat, and it is relevant to the open-standard stablecoin joint venture among industry players. She sees stablecoin use cases in B2B payments, cross-border remittances and P2P, not P2M ('probably a solution looking for a problem').

CFO Ling Hai on the UAE: Mastercard has become the technology provider for the UAE domestic switch through a joint venture with AEP, the Central Bank-owned entity, co-branding with the domestic Jaywan scheme; with a domestic mandate that all debit transactions run through the domestic switch, Mastercard 'will be processing almost 100% of the debit transactions' once implementation is complete and can apply services such as cybersecurity - a playbook for sovereignty agendas that it expects to replicate in other markets.
quarterly_data.figure: almost 100% of UAE debit transactions (once implemented)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ling Hai: services are almost 40% of Mastercard's net revenue - 60% attached to the network and 40% data and insights, consulting and advisory and merchant loyalty - and demand for cyber (identity, fraud, scam prevention, cybersecurity) is strong and broad-based as bad actors use AI; the Recorded Future capability became a new Threat Intelligence product that is attached to, distributed through and priced through the network. Her CFO priorities: top-line growth through front-line investment and acquisitions (core payments, new flows and services), a strong balance sheet, positive operating leverage and returning excess capital.
quarterly_data.figure: services almost 40% of net revenue (60% network-attached)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ling Hai on China: Mastercard's domestic licence was granted two, three years ago and revenue is still 'probably going to be a medium-term opportunity'; it is working with Chinese banks on credit and debit issuance, building acceptance from almost ground zero, and open-loop tap-and-go transit with international cards now works in Shanghai, Beijing, Guangzhou and Shenzhen and has launched in Chengdu; domestic relevance is driving Chinese outbound travel and inbound acceptance in its data.
